issues.issue_description: All recommendations should be addressed by qualified specialists. This is a general recommendation to ensure that any repairs or corrections identified in the report are handled by professionals with the appropriate expertise.
issues.issue_summary: It is recommended that all repairs and corrections identified in this report be performed by qualified specialists to ensure proper and safe execution.

issues.issue_description: Homeowners should obtain required permits before starting renovations. This ensures that any work performed complies with local building codes and regulations.
issues.issue_summary: Before beginning any renovations, homeowners should ensure they obtain all necessary permits from the local authorities.

issues.issue_description: Wood-burning appliances should be inspected by a WETT-certified technician before use. This is a crucial safety measure to prevent fire hazards and ensure proper operation.
issues.issue_summary: A WETT-certified technician should inspect any wood-burning appliances before they are used to ensure they are safe and compliant.

issues.issue_description: A qualified electrician should further evaluate the breaker size compared to the gauge of wire. For example, there is a 40-amp breaker powering a 10-gauge wire. This breaker is also "double-tapped" with an 8-gauge stranded wire, which is generally not permitted. Implication(s): Equipment overheating | Fire hazard. Task: Further evaluation. Time: Immediate.
issues.issue_summary: A 40-amp breaker is improperly connected to a smaller 10-gauge wire and is also double-tapped, creating a significant fire hazard. This requires immediate evaluation and correction by a qualified electrician.

issues.issue_name: Inoperative Gas Fireplace with Incomplete Venting
issues.issue_description: The exhaust vent installation for the gas fireplace is incomplete, which will allow hazardous combustion gases into the home if used. This can be a life safety issue. A technician needs to evaluate the installation compared to the manufacturer's installation requirements and make corrections before the fireplace can be safely used. Task: Correct. Time: Before use.
issues.issue_summary: The basement gas fireplace has an incomplete exhaust vent, posing a life safety hazard from combustion gases. A technician must correct the installation before it can be used.

issues.issue_description: This window is at grade level. To reduce the potential for damage, a window well should be installed. Efforts should be made to keep water/snow away from the window until corrections are made. A window well cover can be a temporary proactive measure. Implication(s): Chance of water damage to structure, finishes and contents | Material deterioration. Task: Correct - Install window well. Time: As soon as reasonably practical.
issues.issue_summary: A window at grade level is missing a window well, increasing the risk of water damage and material deterioration. A window well should be installed.

issues.issue_description: A joist has been notched to accommodate the bathtub plumbing trap. A bathtub can have significant weight when filled with water. A qualified contractor should advise on the appropriate repair method to re-support the joist. Implication(s): Weakened structure. Task: Repair. Time: As soon as possible.
issues.issue_summary: A floor joist in the basement has been improperly notched for plumbing, weakening the structure. A qualified contractor should repair it as soon as possible.

issues.issue_description: An annual maintenance program is recommended for heating and cooling systems to optimize safety, efficiency, comfort, and durability.
issues.issue_summary: An annual maintenance program is recommended for the heating and cooling systems to ensure optimal performance, safety, and longevity.

issues.issue_description: The attic insulation is lower than current standards. The approximate attic/roof insulation amount/value is R-20. Increasing insulation is considered a discretionary improvement that may improve comfort and lower energy bills. Check eligibility for home efficiency rebates. Implication: Increased heating and cooling costs. Task: Improve. Time: Discretionary.
issues.issue_summary: The attic has R-20 insulation, which is below current standards. Adding more insulation is a discretionary improvement that could lower energy costs.

issues.issue_description: Residential traps should be P-type. The current waste plumbing installation (including the dishwasher connection downstream of the trap) should be evaluated by a qualified plumber and corrected. Monitor for odors that may indicate siphoning allowing sewer gases to enter the home. Implication(s): Reduced operability | Fixtures slow to drain. Task: Correct. Time: As soon as reasonably practical.
issues.issue_summary: The kitchen sink has a non-standard (S-type) trap which can lead to siphoning and sewer gas entry. A qualified plumber should evaluate and correct the installation.

issues.issue_description: The stain was checked with a moisture meter after running water in the bathroom above and did not have elevated levels at the time of the inspection. After repairs (i.e. painting) are completed, inspect the area periodically for any changes. Implication(s): Chance of water damage to structure, finishes and contents. Task: Repair, Monitor for future correction. Time: Ongoing (periodically following repairs).
issues.issue_summary: A water stain was found on the living room ceiling. It was dry at the time of inspection, but the area should be repaired and then monitored for any recurrence.
